About Aman

I build growth system
for B2B and D2C companies

If acquisition isn't a system, you're hoping for luck. That lesson has shaped how I think about ICPs, funnels, outbound, paid media, reporting, and retention.

My Story

Meal House showed me why growth needs a system

Before this, I tried being a founder. I started Meal House, a small B2B food business, and ran it for about a year before shutting it down. The product was fine. People liked it. I just didn't know how to find enough of the right customers and keep them coming back.

That's the thing I think about a lot now. If acquisition isn't a system, you're hoping for luck.

For the last five years I've been on the other side of that problem. ICPs, funnels, outbound, paid media, and the kind of reporting that actually tells you something. I've worked on it at Quick Clean, AccountX, and Bertrand & Bernard, across enterprise B2B and D2C.

If you're building something and the growth side feels guessy, send me an email.

Founder Lesson

A good product is not enough if the right customers are not being reached, qualified, and retained through a repeatable system.

Growth Work

ICPs, funnels, outbound, paid media, events, sales enablement, and reporting that connects marketing work to business outcomes.

Where I Help

When growth feels unclear or too dependent on guesswork, I help turn it into a clearer system with better targeting, follow-up, and measurement.

Current Project · In Development
AI Automation · B2B Manufacturing · Receivables-Led GTM

AI GTM Automation
System

A prototype multi-agent automation system designed to reduce repetitive research, enrichment, outreach drafting, event preparation, content monitoring, and RevOps reporting for B2B manufacturing and industrial finance workflows.

6
workflow agents mapped
75%
digital workflow scope
24/7
monitoring-first design
WIP
prototype architecture
Overview

What this system is meant to solve

The Problem
Manual GTM research does not scale cleanly
Research, account enrichment, financial context, outreach drafting, CRM updates, and daily reporting usually sit across different people and spreadsheets. The output becomes slow, inconsistent, and hard to monitor.
The Solution
A coordinated automation layer
The system maps six repeatable workflows into agent-like modules, with one shared operating layer for prospect data, financial signals, engagement events, trial status, and reporting.
Realistic Scope
Digital work first, human approval where needed
Research, scoring, drafts, alerts, summaries, and CRM updates are good automation candidates. Physical events, field activations, and sensitive outbound steps still need human review or execution.
Current Stage
Prototype architecture, not a launched product
This is being positioned as a current build: system design, logic mapping, workflow architecture, and implementation planning for a practical GTM automation stack.
Positioning note: This section avoids client/company names and shows the project as a neutral B2B manufacturing automation prototype, not as a fully deployed autonomous product.
Agent Map

Six workflow agents in the system

Each module represents one repeatable GTM task area. The goal is not to remove judgement — it is to remove repetitive execution and surface better decisions faster.

Agent 01 / Intel
Intelligence & Enrichment
Collects public account context, financial indicators, company details, sector signals, and enrichment fields. Produces a cleaned account profile for the rest of the system.
Fully digital
Agent 02 / Outreach
Outreach Drafting
Generates personalised email, WhatsApp, and call-script drafts based on the account profile. Human review stays in place before sensitive outbound actions.
Human approval
Agent 03 / Events
Event & Association Prep
Tracks relevant trade shows, associations, attendee lists, and meeting opportunities. Builds briefing notes so the human operator walks in prepared.
Partially automated
Agent 04 / Field
Field Activation Dispatcher
Handles QR triggers, location-based alerts, follow-up routing, and campaign reporting for offline activations. Physical execution remains human-led.
Dispatcher role
Agent 05 / Content
Market & Content Monitor
Monitors public market updates and industry signals, then drafts reactive content angles, email ideas, and leadership summaries.
Fully digital
Agent 06 / RevOps
CRM & Reporting Manager
Syncs activity into CRM or sheets, updates scores, flags dormant opportunities, and creates daily summaries for sales or leadership review.
Fully digital

Why this works better: it keeps the automation story ambitious but believable — decisions, review gates, and compliance-sensitive steps are clearly separated.
System Flow

How the workflow moves

This is the practical logic of the build: a trigger comes in, the system enriches and scores it, a human reviews sensitive actions, and approved output gets pushed back into the operating layer.

Prototype logic flowShared data layer · event-driven routing · human review gates
1. Trigger

Schedule, manual signal, new account upload, market update, event list, or CRM status change.

2. Enrich

Collect public account context, financial signals, contact fields, sector data, and source notes.

3. Score

Assign urgency, fit, account priority, and suggested next action using rule-based logic plus AI assistance.

4. Draft

Create outreach angles, call notes, email drafts, content ideas, or event briefing documents.

5. Sync

Push approved output into CRM, Sheets, Slack/email briefings, or the next workflow queue.

Quick Clean · Case Study 01

Commercial Laundry Growth
in India

Quick Clean, founded in 2011, was working to shift the perception of commercial laundry from a generic vendor service to a structured operating partner for hotels and hospitals. When I joined in 2024, the marketing challenge was to build ICP clarity, sharpen messaging, and create a multi-channel demand generation engine from scratch.

40%
MQL to SQL
Conversion Lift
B2B GTM Hospitality + Healthcare ICP & Segmentation Multi-Channel Engine ~30 SQLs / Quarter ₹1 Cr Annual Budget 10+ Events
Overview
Business Context
Quick Clean provides outsourced commercial laundry services to hotels and hospitals in India. The category is largely unorganized — most properties rely on in-house laundry or informal local vendors. The opportunity was to reposition Quick Clean as a professional, zero-capex operating partner.
Marketing Challenge
No structured ICP, segmentation, or qualification framework. Messaging was generic — not tailored to hospitality vs healthcare, or by stakeholder role. Enterprise deals involved multiple decision-makers with different pain points and buying criteria.
Aman's Role
Marketing & Communication Manager. Responsible for ICP definition, GTM strategy, messaging, campaign execution, event presence, outbound systems, and funnel qualification. Did not handle operations, pricing negotiations, or customer success.
Primary ICP
Hospitality: Hotels with 150+ rooms (greenfield and brownfield). Healthcare: Hospitals with 250+ beds. Messaging varied by segment and stakeholder role within each segment.
Channels Used
Event marketing (Hotelier India, GM Summit), LinkedIn outreach, cold email sequences, WhatsApp follow-ups, and segment-specific landing pages and website content.
Primary Outcome
40% improvement in MQL to SQL conversion rate. Generated ~30 SQLs per quarter and managed a ₹1 Cr annual budget across events, outbound, sales collateral, and marketing tools. Built a repeatable, structured qualification framework.
Breakdown

Challenge · Strategy · Impact

Growth Challenge
  • Commercial laundry was an under-structured category — perception needed to shift from "vendor" to "partner"
  • Hotels and hospitals had entirely different buying triggers, pain points, and stakeholder hierarchies
  • Enterprise deals involved multiple decision-makers across departments
  • Messaging had to vary across greenfield hotels, brownfield hotels, and hospital segments
  • No structured segmentation, ICP definition, or qualification framework existed
Strategy
  • Defined ICP by property type, stage, room/bed count, laundry volume, cost pressure, and hygiene requirements
  • Built stakeholder-specific messaging for Hotel Owners, GMs, CFOs, EHKs, Purchase, and Engineering teams
  • Created segment-specific outreach: greenfield, brownfield, healthcare
  • Executed event marketing at industry-specific forums with direct decision-maker access
  • Built cold email and LinkedIn outreach aligned with ICP qualification criteria
  • Used WhatsApp follow-ups and case-study-led nurturing for stakeholder re-engagement
Business Impact
  • 40% improvement in MQL to SQL conversion rate
  • ~30 SQLs per quarter generated through events, outbound, sales collateral, and marketing tools
  • Managed a ₹1 Cr annual budget and built a 5-member marketing team from the ground up
  • Led event-led GTM across 10+ events, including a ₹60L/year ITP Media partnership across 4 events
  • Built a repeatable qualification framework and multi-channel acquisition engine
  • Improved funnel quality — fewer unqualified conversations, more structured pipeline
  • Helped shift marketing from generic awareness to structured, segment-specific acquisition

ICP Framework

Commercial Laundry ICP

ICP Segmentation Framework
Commercial Laundry ICP
Hospitality — Hotels
Qualification Filter
150+ rooms minimum Greenfield or Brownfield High daily linen volume
Pain Points
Capex avoidance Space constraints Linen hygiene & consistency
Stakeholders Targeted
OwnerGM CFOEHK PurchaseEngineering
Lead Value Logic
150 rooms × ~6 kg/room/day = ~900 kg daily · ~₹30/kg → ~₹27,000/day per property. Used to prioritize high-volume accounts at qualification.
Healthcare — Hospitals
Qualification Filter
250+ beds minimum High-volume linen flow Infection control priority
Pain Points
Infection control standards Hygiene compliance Cost per kg efficiency
Stakeholders Targeted
AdminOperations PurchaseFinance
Lead Value Logic
Healthcare-grade processing ~₹55–60/kg. Infection-control compliance was the primary qualifying signal — not just volume alone.

How the Growth System Was Built

Email Sequence Logic
Follow-Up Cadence for Senior Decision-Makers

UHNI and senior hospitality decision-makers cannot be followed up repeatedly like low-ticket leads. Cadence was controlled, context-led, and spaced to respect their seniority.

1
Intro + Problem Frame
Segment-specific opening tied to their exact operational challenge (capex, space, hygiene). No generic pitch.
2
Case Study or Proof
Relevant hotel or hospital reference. Let proof do the persuading — not pressure.
3
Value Reframe
Cost-per-kg comparison or capex savings angle, tailored to CFO/Owner profile.
4
Soft Close / Check-In
Light-touch follow-up with a direct ask — "Is this worth a 20-minute call?" Spaced 7–10 days from previous.
ICP Qualification Framework
Structured Lead Scoring Logic
Leads were qualified on a combination of property type, size, current laundry setup, pain signal, and stakeholder seniority. This prevented wasted sales conversations with under-qualified accounts.

High priority: 150+ room hotels with in-house laundry pain, or 250+ bed hospitals with hygiene compliance urgency.
Medium priority: Pre-opening greenfield hotels where laundry setup was still being decided.
Low priority: Properties with established contracts already in place, or those below minimum size threshold.

Snapshot metrics: 3K total sent · 40% open rate · 3.2% click rate · 4.5% reply rate · 2 opportunities | $14,000.

Events & Field Demand Generation

Hospitality events were used as a direct SQL channel

Quick Clean collaborated with and sponsored ITP Media hospitality events to reach hotel owners, General Managers, and senior operators in the exact environments where buying conversations were already happening. This sat inside 10+ event-led GTM motions, including a ₹60L/year ITP Media partnership across 4 events.

ITP Media Collaborations

Direct access to hotel decision-makers

We participated in hospitality events hosted at large five-star hotels. Instead of opening with a direct laundry pitch, conversations started around industry context, hotel operations, guest experience, and cost pressure — then moved naturally into how Quick Clean could support laundry operations.

GM Summit GM Awards Hotelier India Awards Global Design & Development
Preparation Window

25–30 days before the event

Vendor coordinationPersonally called vendors, discussed booth requirements, negotiated setup needs, and aligned deliverables.
Booth planningFinalised booth structure, expected footfall, collateral requirements, team movement, and onsite flow.
Collateral readinessPrepared brochures, company profile, pitch material, and talking points before the event day.
01Booth setup

Booth and collaterals were usually set up around 24 hours before the event.

02Networking first

Team conversations started with industry context before moving into the laundry solution.

03Stakeholder pitch

Personally handled on-ground conversations with hotel owners, GMs, and senior stakeholders, positioning Quick Clean’s BOO, valet, leasing, and linen solutions around operational pain points.

04Lead capture

Visiting cards were collected and notes were recorded in CRM or Excel for accurate follow-up.

05Next-day follow-up

Email, calls, and meeting follow-ups started the next day based on the conversation context.

Lead impact: Event-led GTM across 10+ events, including a ₹60L/year ITP Media partnership across 4 events, contributed to ~30 SQLs per quarter alongside email outreach, LinkedIn, website interest, sales collateral, and other outbound channels.
Retail Open House

Retail open houses were rebuilt into leadership-led customer forums

Retail Open House Program

Converted office visits into curated feedback and relationship sessions

Earlier, retail customers were invited to the office and mostly attended by a supervisor. I changed the format into a more structured open house program by segmenting customers, narrowing down large lists, sending targeted invitations to the right people, and bringing them into sessions with Quick Clean leadership.

BeforeInvitation-based office visits with broad customer lists, supervisor-led handling, limited leadership visibility, and informal feedback capture.
Audience buildingCreated sharper customer segments, filtered the lists, and invited the most relevant retail customers based on priority, relationship stage, and feedback value.
Leadership sessionBuilt 1 to 2 hour CEO/founder-led sessions with management involvement, online or offline formats, partner and distributor executive participation, lunch, Q&A, and direct problem-listening.
Feedback loopCaptured customer concerns, converted them into clear action points, and worked with internal teams and partners to improve the customer experience after the session.

AccountX · Case Study 02

Building a Global Sales &
Marketing Engine from Scratch

AccountX was a CA, accounting, tax, compliance, and business advisory firm expanding across global markets. There was no structured acquisition system, no outbound process, and no market-specific messaging when I joined. The entire GTM foundation — website messaging, ICP research, email infrastructure, and outbound systems — was built in 15–20 days.

70–80
Qualified Leads
per Month
Global GTM 15–20 Day Setup 10 Markets LinkedIn + Cold Email Country-wise ICP
Overview
Business Context
AccountX provides CA, accounting, tax, compliance, and virtual CFO services to businesses across global markets. The firm was expanding internationally but had no acquisition infrastructure — no structured outbound, no messaging framework, and no country-wise positioning.
Marketing Challenge
Multiple target markets with different compliance needs, buyer pain points, and service expectations. Needed to simultaneously build the website, pitch decks, proposals, email infrastructure, ICP research, and outbound playbook — with no prior foundation.
Aman's Role
GTM strategy, website messaging, service positioning, pitch decks, proposals, outbound infrastructure, ICP research, LinkedIn outreach, cold email campaigns, SEO strategy, and Google Search Ads. Did not handle accounting delivery, legal compliance execution, sales closure, or negotiations.
Target Buyers
Indian founders and SMEs going global, foreign companies entering India, existing global businesses needing accounting cleanup or virtual CFO, and fundraising-stage companies needing investor-readiness support.
Channels Used
LinkedIn Sales Navigator, cold email (with warm-up infrastructure), SEO, Google Search Ads, LinkedIn Ads, retargeting, and webinars for education-led demand generation.
Primary Outcome
Scaled outbound to 70–80 qualified leads per month. Built a repeatable acquisition system. Helped move the firm from founder-led selling toward structured, multi-channel acquisition across 10 global markets.
Breakdown

Challenge · Strategy · Impact

Growth Challenge
  • No acquisition system, outbound process, or structured messaging at the start
  • Multiple markets meant different compliance needs, buyer pain points, and service expectations
  • Needed website messaging, pitch decks, proposals, and market-specific positioning — all simultaneously
  • Target buyers ranged from Indian founders going global to foreign companies entering India
  • Had to shift from generic accounting positioning to sharper, market-specific acquisition
Strategy
  • Built the core GTM foundation in 15–20 days: website messaging, service positioning, pitch decks, proposals, and outbound assets
  • Set up email warm-up infrastructure and cold outbound sequences
  • Built country-wise ICP research and market-specific messaging for 10 markets
  • Used LinkedIn Sales Navigator and cold email as primary outbound channels
  • Supported demand generation via SEO, Google Search Ads, LinkedIn Ads, and retargeting
  • Lead nurturing via client proof, case-study-led messaging, and pain-point-based follow-ups
Business Impact
  • Scaled outbound to 70–80 qualified leads per month
  • Built a repeatable outbound acquisition system
  • Created a stronger global positioning and messaging foundation
  • Improved sales conversations through sharper proposals and pitch decks
  • Helped move from founder-led selling toward structured acquisition
  • Supported market expansion across 10 countries

Email Sequence Logic
Outbound Cadence for Global B2B Compliance Services

Compliance and advisory services require trust before action. Sequences were structured around education, relevance, and proof — not repeated pressure.

1
Problem-Led Opener
Market-specific pain framing — e.g., "Setting up a US LLC as an Indian founder" or "India compliance for foreign entities."
2
Service + Proof
Relevant case example or client type reference. What was the situation, what was done, what was the outcome.
3
Country-Specific Value
Compliance nuances by market — UAE free zone vs mainland, Singapore incorporation requirements, India GST setup.
4
Soft Call-to-Action
Low-friction ask — "Worth a 15-minute call to see if this fits your situation?" Spaced 5–7 days from previous touchpoint.
GTM Foundation Built
What Was Created in 15–20 Days
The core infrastructure was created fast — not a full mature system, but a working foundation that could be scaled.

Website messaging — Service pages, positioning copy, and market-specific landing pages.
Sales messaging — Segment-specific positioning for Indian founders, foreign companies, and existing global businesses.
Proposal logic — Structured buyer-stage messaging aligned to service type and decision context.
Email infrastructure — Domain warm-up, deliverability setup, and outbound sequences.
ICP research — Country-wise buyer profiles, pain points, and compliance context.

Performance Marketing &
E-commerce CRO

Managed performance marketing and Shopify CRO for Bertrand & Bernard across three businesses: a pet store, a dental clinic, and a beauty products brand. The focus was on improving ROAS through better audience targeting, landing page quality, A/B testing, and conversion journey improvements while reducing cost per acquisition across Meta campaigns.

ROAS on
Performance Campaigns

Overview
Business Context
Bertrand & Bernard operated Shopify-led e-commerce brands. The challenge was to improve the efficiency and quality of paid acquisition — not just spend more, but get better returns from existing and new budget by improving the full conversion journey.
Marketing Challenge
ROAS was below target. Ad creative, audience targeting, landing page quality, and checkout flow all needed improvement. CPA was too high relative to average order value. No structured A/B testing process existed.
Aman's Role
Managed Meta Ads campaigns, executed Shopify CRO work, built and tested landing pages, implemented A/B testing cadence, and optimized the conversion journey end-to-end. Did not handle logistics, inventory, or customer service.
Channels Used
Meta Ads (Facebook + Instagram), Google Ads (secondary support), Shopify landing pages, A/B testing tools, heatmap and session analysis, and conversion rate optimization across product pages and checkout.
Primary Outcome
Up to 2.5× ROAS on performance campaigns. Improved CTR, reduced CPA, and built a more structured testing and optimization cadence. Improved landing page conversion through iterative A/B testing.

What Changed

Why the performance shifted in H2 2023

The improvement was not just a bigger budget story. The account review points to a mix of cleaner campaign structure, stronger conversion signals, better campaign hygiene, and more focused market expansion. The safest read is that H2 2023 improved because the account became easier for Google Ads to optimize and budget was pushed toward stronger lead potential.

01
Tracking and signal quality improved

Earlier conversion data looked limited or inconsistent. As tracking and lead-form signals improved, Smart Bidding had better data to optimize against, which helped measured conversions rise sharply.

02
Smart Bidding had more learning data

The legacy campaigns kept Maximize Conversions, but by H2 the algorithm had more conversion history. That likely helped it find better users without needing a major bidding overhaul.

03
Weak tests were pruned

Underperforming campaigns and experiments were reduced, paused, or replaced. This helped stop budget bleed and kept more spend inside campaigns that had stronger conversion behavior.

04
New market expansion was tested

A dedicated New Zealand push was introduced in July, while USA activity was also scaled. This added new audience pools instead of relying only on the earlier Australia and Bangkok setup.

05
Budget moved toward higher intent

Spend was not increased aggressively. The bigger change was where the budget went: more emphasis on campaigns and channels that could produce trackable lead actions.

06
The result was efficiency, not just volume

Impressions were lower in the proof account view, yet conversions increased and cost per conversion dropped. That points to better traffic quality and improved measurement, not just more reach.

Measurement note: Conversion numbers are shown as measured Google Ads conversions. Because tracking was improved during the year, the lift reflects both stronger campaign performance and better conversion measurement, not a pure claim of business growth.

Meal House · Case Study 04

Building a B2B Food Services
Business from Scratch

Before GTM strategies and acquisition funnels, I founded Meal House — a B2B food services business serving industrial companies across Bawal, Dharuhera, and Bhiwadi. No playbook. Just figuring out pricing, vendor management, logistics, and how to earn repeat corporate clients.

3+
Corporate
Clients Served
2
Operational
Models
3
Industrial Belt
Locations
B2B Operations Industrial Food Services Vendor Management Client Acquisition Founder Story
Overview
Business Context
Meal House was a B2B food services business targeting industrial companies across the Rajasthan-Haryana industrial belt. The segment had a clear gap: factory workers and office staff needed reliable, quality food but most options were informal and inconsistent.
The Challenge
No established playbook. Had to figure out pricing, vendor sourcing, logistics, and repeatable delivery from zero. Corporate clients demanded consistency, hygiene, and punctuality — margin for error was low.
Aman's Role
Founder. Responsible for business model design, client acquisition, vendor coordination, pricing, logistics, operations, and repeat service delivery — the full business cycle, end-to-end.
Target Market
Industrial companies, factories, and corporate campuses across Bawal, Dharuhera, and Bhiwadi with recurring food service requirements for employees and staff.
Operational Models
Model 01: Central Kitchen with own delivery logistics. Model 02: On-premise kitchen setup inside company premises for larger clients needing dedicated, in-house food service infrastructure.
Key Learning
Shaped deep understanding of customer pain, pricing, operations discipline, and retention — foundational thinking that now drives how I approach GTM, unit economics, and growth strategy.
Breakdown

Challenge · Execution · Learning

The Challenge
  • No established market maps or vendor networks to rely on
  • Corporate clients demanded hygiene, consistency, and punctuality
  • Pricing had to balance thin margins, vendor costs, and competitive rates
  • Logistics and delivery reliability were critical to client retention
  • Building trust with procurement and admin decision-makers took persistent effort
Execution
  • Sourced and qualified local vendors for central kitchen supply and quality control
  • Designed two operational models based on client size and requirements
  • Built client acquisition through direct outreach, referrals, and on-site demos
  • Managed full delivery logistics including timing, consistency, and issue resolution
  • Handled client retention through regular check-ins and service reliability
Business Learning
  • Customer pain is best understood by being close to operations, not just data
  • Pricing must account for real unit economics, not just competitive benchmarking
  • Retention is built through execution discipline, not just relationship management
  • Scaling requires systemisation before growth — you can't hire out of broken ops
  • This experience informs how I think about GTM, product-market fit, and sustainable growth
Coverage

Industrial Belt Operations

Meal House served companies across three industrial clusters in the Rajasthan-Haryana corridor — a dense, underserved geography with high demand for reliable B2B food services.
